npcs.name: Ottar Woodcutter
npcs.idle: I cut trees. That's all. That's all I ever did.

npcs.name: Sunniva
npcs.idle: (She opens her mouth, and nothing comes out. Tears roll down her face, silently, and she points west.)

npcs.name: Asgerd
npcs.idle: My husband hasn't slept a night through since winter. Something rides him.

npcs.name: Grimkel the Sleepless
npcs.idle: Hoofbeats. Every night. On my chest.

quests.title: The Willow's Voice
quests.offer:
I felled a willow in the western wood this spring. A big old weeper. The next morning my daughter Sunniva woke and couldn't speak. She cries all day - no sound, just tears.

The seeress says the willows took her voice in payment. I'd give them anything. I'd give them my axe. Will you [help her]? Talk to her if you like. She can't answer.
quests.summary: Ottar felled an old willow, and the next morning his daughter woke unable to speak, only weep.

steps.say: (She takes your hand and presses something into it: a willow leaf, still green. Then she points west, toward the weeping grove, and shakes her head hard, and points again.)

steps.goal: Go to the weeping willow grove in the west
steps.text: The willows weep sap like rain. Under the sound of it, very faintly, a little girl's voice humming.
Each one that falls stops humming. The humming moves deeper in.

steps.goal: Find the stump of the willow Ottar felled
steps.text: Ottar's axe-marks, clean and deep. The sap has run down the stump and set in shapes like letters: GIVE BACK WHAT WAS TAKEN.
The Elder Willow bows, groaning, to the ground. In the hollow of its trunk lies a little knot of heartwood that sings in a child's voice.

stages.name: the Elder Willow
stages.announce: The biggest willow in the grove opens eyes of knotted bark. 'THE AXE-MAN TOOK OUR SISTER. WE TOOK HIS DAUGHTER'S SONG.'

steps.goal: Bring the singing heartwood to Ottar
steps.say:
That's - that's her voice. In the wood. Gods.

The seeress says I can [plant the heartwood] at the stump, and swear never to fell a tree again, and the voice comes home. I'd have to find other work. I'm forty. I've only ever cut trees.

Or I [burn it] in the hearth, and the voice comes home tonight, and the willows remember us forever.

options.say: Then I'll plant it. And swear. And learn to - I don't know. Keep bees. Sunniva always wanted bees.
Burn it. Tonight. I want to hear her laugh tonight, not next spring. Let the trees remember.

planted.text: She sang this morning. Take this - she wants you to.

burned.text: She talks now. Doesn't stop. The willows by the house have started to lean toward it. Take this.

quests.title: Hoofbeats in the Night
quests.offer:
My Grimkel hasn't slept a night since winter. Something rides him - a mora, the old women say. A night-mare. It sits on his chest and he can't breathe, can't wake. He's wasting.

The moras dance in the southern wood, by the old shrine. Will you [stop it]? Ask [Grimkel] what he sees, if he's awake enough to tell you.

topics.Grimkel: He's by the hall. Sitting up. He won't lie down any more.

quests.summary: Something rides Asgerd's husband every night - a mora, a night-mare - and he is wasting away.

steps.say: A woman. Pale. Riding a black horse that's also her. Every night, on my chest, galloping. She says I'm hers. She has a [bridle] of hair - my hair. She cut it while I slept.

steps.goal: Go to the moras' dancing grounds in the south
steps.text: Women dance in a ring, too light on their feet - and some of them have hooves.
They dissolve into black mist. The ring breaks open. Riders on black horses circle further in.

steps.goal: Search the centre of the ring
steps.text: A bridle of braided hair - several bridles. Each a different colour. One is grey-brown, like Grimkel's.
The Mare-Queen's horse-half crumbles into ash, then her woman-half. Every bridle in the ring goes limp.

stages.name: the Mare-Queen
stages.announce: A rider on a horse that is also herself gallops out of the dark. 'Give me back my reins!'

steps.goal: Bring the bridle back to Asgerd
steps.say:
Is that his? His hair, in a bridle?

The old women say whoever holds the bridle can ride the mora's dreams - into anyone's sleep. Grimkel wants it. He wants to ride into the dreams of the man who cheated him at the spring fair. He's never been like this.

[Burn it]. Please. Or [give it to him], if you think he's earned his revenge. I can't stop him.

options.say: Thank you. Oh, thank you. ...Listen. He's snoring. He's SNORING.
...So be it. He's sleeping now. Smiling. I don't like the smile.

burned.text: Take this. We'll both sleep tonight.
